sections.title: Model overview and intended purpose
sections.text: Python Random Forest (model_id: python-random-forest) is a benchmark model for internal analysis and is not used in decisions; it serves as a comparison model rather than the migration candidate. It predicts the binary target default.payment.next.month using the UCI Default of Credit Card Clients dataset (30,000 records of credit-card clients in Taiwan, payment history April to September 2005), which is public demonstration data and not representative of a UK bank's current portfolio. The business owner, intended use and decision context are not documented, and the business purpose and target variable are recorded as inferred. The model is assigned risk tier 3.

sections.title: Algorithm and methodology
sections.text: The model is a scikit-learn RandomForestClassifier with n_estimators=150, random_state=seed (default 42), n_jobs=-1 and class_weight="balanced" to address an expected default rate of about 22%; other hyperparameters use library defaults. It uses 21 predictors (LIMIT_BAL, EDUCATION, MARRIAGE, PAY_0 and PAY_2 to PAY_6, BILL_AMT1 to BILL_AMT6, PAY_AMT1 to PAY_AMT6), with ID, SEX and AGE excluded and SEX and AGE treated as fairness-only attributes. Preprocessing renames columns, drops ID and rows with missing values, validates the official dataset (30,000 rows, 25 columns, no missing values, default rate between 0.20 and 0.24), casts the target to int, and applies no scaling or encoding. Data is split with a stratified 80/20 train/test split (random_state=42 by default), shared with the R legacy model.

sections.title: Limitations and assumptions
sections.text: Hyperparameters are fixed with no tuning shown in the code, and the rationale for n_estimators=150 and class_weight=balanced is not documented; no operational decision threshold is documented. The model_identity hash and coefficient extraction support only the Statsmodels candidate, not this model, and if the demo fixture is used instead of the UCI data the model trains on synthetic data with only 3 predictors. Performance metrics, validation results, acceptance criteria, fairness and monitoring results, and prediction PSI are not documented (the results fields are empty). Also not documented are the production data loader, how the train fraction is set at the call site, the interpretability approach, model version, approval status, deployment and retraining schedule.
